reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from July to September 2026 (E-07), and since tariff rates did not change (E-02) and most disputed bills carry ACTUAL, non-estimated reads rather than ESTIMATED ones (1785 vs 1240, E-03), the surge is not explained by a tariff change or by field/AMI read-collection failure. The dominant supported mechanism is a billing-side defect in the import/calculation/validation step that turns accepted actual reads into wrong bills, driving the dispute increase (H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-DEFECT).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from July to September 2026, reaching 1260 tickets (E-07). The dominant supported mechanism: billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 and comparing raw register values directly against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware v4.2 AMI meters (which report in 0.1 m3 units vs v3.x meters' m3 units, E-14) as ~10x true consumption, causing billing import to reject 1184 of 1240 valid, before-cutoff AMI reads as HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12) and forcing estimate substitution that produces wrong/estimated bills, driving the ESTIMATED-dispute portion of the surge.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
